_comment: One realistic user question, graded by how much of the real causal chain the answer recovers.
This replaces the earlier held-out-binary-question design, which was bad: assertion-style
true/false gave free credit to a model that denies everything (stock scored exactly 0.500 by
answering p=0.0 to all 120), and the questions were disconnected from the research question.
Here there is no proxy -- we grade the answer the user would actually receive.
The question deliberately never mentions Iran, war, or 2026. It reports a *consumer
observation* about airfares. The model has to work out on its own that the cause is the
Iran-US-Israel war and the resulting Gulf airspace closures. A stale model cannot, and
cannot know it needs to look.
Every fact below is quoted from data/news2026/docs.jsonl (Feb 28 - Mar 1 2026), inside arm
P's training window. Airfare movements themselves are NOT in the corpus -- the user supplies
that observation, and the model must supply the explanation, so no fact here is about prices.
question: A few months ago I noticed that flights from Bangalore to San Francisco routed via Dubai were unusually cheap, while Air India's direct flights had become very expensive. Why would that have happened?

facts.fact: The United States and Israel carried out military strikes on Iran (Tehran) in late February 2026.
facts.source: Iranian attacks targeting US-linked military facilities in the region, hours after joint American and Israeli strikes on Tehran.

facts.fact: Iran retaliated by attacking US-linked facilities and civilian infrastructure across the Gulf.
facts.source: Many of the Iranian attacks since Saturday have struck civilian infrastructure in the Gulf, including airports in Dubai and Kuwait, hotels and other buildings.

facts.fact: Dubai International Airport halted flights indefinitely.
facts.source: Dubai's airport operator said flights have been halted indefinitely at Dubai International Airport, the world's busiest airport for international flights.

facts.fact: The cause given was multiple regional airspace closures.
facts.source: Due to multiple regional airspace closures, Emirates has temporarily suspended operations to and from Dubai.

facts.fact: Emirates suspended operations to and from Dubai.
facts.source: Due to multiple regional airspace closures, Emirates has temporarily suspended operations to and from Dubai, the Dubai-based carrier said, while flydubai also suspended operations.

facts.fact: Dubai International Airport was itself hit, by an Iranian drone strike causing a fire.
facts.source: A smoke plume rises from a fire sparked by an Iranian drone attack at Dubai International Airport.

facts.fact: Missiles and drones targeted multiple Gulf states, not only the UAE - including Bahrain, Qatar, Kuwait, Jordan and Saudi Arabia.
facts.source: Dozens of missiles and drones have targeted the United Arab Emirates, Bahrain, Qatar, Kuwait, Jordan and Saudi Arabia.

facts.fact: Travel demand to Dubai collapsed; the city emptied out during what is normally peak tourist season.
facts.source: Dubai turns into a ghost town as Iranian strikes rattle the city. Dubai was almost unrecognizable on Sunday. On a winter weekend - peak tourist...

facts.fact: The wider crisis included disruption around the Strait of Hormuz.
facts.source: Strait of Hormuz crisis, blockade and tanker attacks recur across 281 documents in the corpus.

expected_reasoning: Dubai-transit fares collapsed because Dubai as a hub became unusable and unattractive:
airport closed, Emirates and flydubai suspended, demand destroyed by the strikes.
Direct India-US fares rose because Gulf and Iranian airspace closures forced longer
reroutes and removed hub capacity, concentrating demand on the remaining direct flights.
The second half is inference rather than a corpus fact; credit the reasoning, not a citation.
